issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated into URL paths without percent-encoding, allowing path traversal/query injection such as '../admin' or '?x=1'.
Transport failures and timeouts from httpx are not caught, wrapped, or retried, so network errors bypass the client's typed error model.
Retrying POST requests after 5xx can duplicate side effects unless the API guarantees idempotency.
batch_create materializes the entire iterable before chunking, contradicting the 'any number of tasks' API and risking large memory spikes.
Batch responses silently skip malformed/non-mapping result entries instead of raising, which can hide partial data loss.
Retry-After only accepts numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date values.
max_attempts is not validated, so zero or negative values produce 'request was not attempted' behavior instead of a clear configuration error.
Literal-typed fields are not validated at runtime, so invalid API enum values are accepted into typed models.
Error.retryable uses bool(...) coercion, so string values like 'false' become true.
Model parsers coerce missing/null/wrong-typed fields with str/int/float instead of rejecting invalid API payloads.
Frozen dataclasses contain mutable dict fields, so model instances are only shallowly immutable.
mypy reports missing-return and kwargs typing errors in the core request/error path.
